title: a wrong-length literal in the right operand of or, after a variable that holds True, runs at -O1 and above and is rejected at -O0
compiler: prints `True` at -O1, -O2 and -O3, the default, and with mojo run and -D ASSERT=all; -O0 rejects it with "function instantiation failed" and the note "constraint failed: expected 1 elements in the SIMD list literal, found 3". The comparison alone, and the same or with `var t = False`, are rejected at every level
fixed: rejects it at every level, as -O0 does and as every level rejects the comparison alone (noMatchingInit)

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular
